name: Niu Niu (Ox-Ox, Bullfighting)
description: Niu Niu (literally 'Ox Ox') is a popular gambling card game originating from Southern China and widely played in Southeast Asia. It is a banking game where players receive five cards and must split them into a three-card set (totaling a multiple of 10) and a two-card hand. The value of the two-card hand determines the strength of the 'Ox'. It is known for its fast pace, significant multipliers on high hands, and its ubiquity in Asian casinos and social gatherings.

overview.description: Niu Niu (literally 'Ox Ox') is a popular gambling card game originating from Southern China and widely played in Southeast Asia. It is a banking game where players receive five cards and must split them into a three-card set (totaling a multiple of 10) and a two-card hand. The value of the two-card hand determines the strength of the 'Ox'. It is known for its fast pace, significant multipliers on high hands, and its ubiquity in Asian casinos and social gatherings.

history.origins: Rooted in traditional Chinese gambling games like Pai Gow and Mahjong, Niu Niu was adapted for Western playing cards in the early 20th century. The 'Ox' (Niu) symbolizes strength and good luck.
timeline: 1900s: Traditional Niu Niu rules emerge in rural China.
1980s: Rapid expansion into casinos in Macau, Cambodia, and Vietnam.
2010s: Online Niu Niu (also called Bullfighting) becomes a massive industry in mobile gaming.
Present: One of the most common 'Casino' card games in the Chinese-speaking world.
history.cultural: Commonly played during Chinese New Year as a social luck-testing game.
history.evolution: The game's scoring evolved to include 'Multipliers' (e.g., Niu Niu pays 3x) to increase betting volatility.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Rank: King > Queen > Jack > 10 > 9... > Ace. Suits: Spade > Heart > Club > Diamond.
setup.dealing: Each player (and the banker) receives 5 cards.

rules.objective: Beat the banker by forming a higher Niu value: split your five cards into a three-card set (sum must be a multiple of 10) and a two-card hand; the units digit of the two-card sum is your rank (0–9). Higher rank wins; Niu Niu (0) beats all point hands; ties are broken by highest single card.
rules.gameplay: One banker and multiple players. Each receives five cards. Players split their five cards into a three-card set (total must be a multiple of 10) and a two-card hand. The two-card hand's point value (units digit only, e.g. 17 counts as 7) is the hand rank. Banker does the same. Compare each player's hand to the banker: higher point value wins. Niu Niu (both three- and two-card parts total zero) is the highest normal hand. Ties broken by highest single card. Equal bet pays 1:1 (minus 5% commission on wins); Double bet pays 1:1 for 1-6 points, 2:1 for 7-9, 3:1 for Niu Niu (player can lose up to 3x on Double).
keyRules: Split five cards into three-card (multiple of 10) and two-card hand; units digit of two-card sum is your Niu value (0-9).
Higher Niu value beats lower; Niu Niu (0+0) beats all point hands. Tie-break by highest card.
Equal bet: 1:1 win/loss, 5% commission on wins. Double bet: 1-6 pays 1:1, 7-9 pays 2:1, Niu Niu pays 3:1; lose up to 3x stake.
Face cards count as 10. Aces typically 1 or 11 by variant.

strategy.basic: Identify the 10-multiples immediately. Face cards are your best friends because they count as 10, making it very easy to hit the 20 or 30 mark for your foundation. If you have two 10s and a 5, you need another 5 to make a foundation; if you don't have it, you likely have 'No Niu'.
strategy.intermediate: The 'High Card' Tie-Breaker: If both you and the banker have the same Niu value (e.g., Niu 7), the winner is decided by the highest individual card. Therefore, having a King increases your win probability significantly even if your hand point-value is mediocre.
strategy.advanced: Bankroll Management: Because Niu Niu often features 'Double' or 'Triple' payouts for Niu 7 or higher, a single bad round as the banker can wipe out your entire stack. Strategic players often choose to 'Bank' only when they have enough capital to survive a Niu Niu sweep.
tips: In many variations, the 'King of Spades' is the absolute tie-breaker. If you hold it, you can never lose a tie.
If playing online, watch for 'Super Niu Niu' side bets that pay for 5-card-face-card hands (Five Dukes).
